name: Humans
homeland: the Crownlands and every reach of Aurelith
summary: The makers of the current age. Short-lived, restless, and everywhere. Humans rebuilt the Crownlands after the Sundering, struck the first coins, and hold the canonical Chorus. They forget the song faster than any other people — and remember fear longest.
appearance: As varied as the regions they inhabit: fair and freckled in the Dusk Reach, sun-browned in the Crownlands, ash-pale in the shadow of the Quiet.
Hair worn long in the east, shaved at the temples in the west; the white silk of Velkash is the common pride of the wealthy.
temperament: ambitious, adaptable, reverent to ritual, quick to forget

society.government: Kingdoms and elected reeves; the Crownlands' council is the oldest standing institution
society.family: Households of three generations; oaths bind families as much as blood

religion: The Chorus in its canonical form. Solvane chief in the Crownlands; regional variation everywhere. Ithyn's cult outlawed but alive in the Hollow Mile.

relations.note: The deep-folk's steel and the human grain feed each other; the deep-folk find human haste tiresome.
The greenfolk are old and slow; humans petition them for lore and receive silence.
Caravan trade thrives, but the hollowborn's forbidden writings worry the Reeve's court.

notes: Humans are the only species with no unique deity — they took the whole Chorus and made it theirs.
Their speed of forgetting is central to the age: the Sundering is history to them, myth to the greenfolk, a scar to the deep-folk.
